title: School of War or School of Battle? Educating for an Uncertain Future
gist: West Point historians Ferguson and Rogers argue against rebalancing US professional military education toward technical warfighting proficiency (AI, drones, multi-domain ops) at the expense of history and strategy, because curricular time is zero-sum and nobody can predict the character of the next war. They propose protecting history and strategy hours by statute in Title 10 to avoid repeating America's pattern of winning battles but losing wars.

insights.claim: Unless service-college study hours increase, spending more time on the technical dimensions of war's changing character must mean less time on war's unchanging nature and the eternals of strategy.
insights.speaker: Michael P. Ferguson and Clifford J. Rogers
insights.so_what: Frames the trade-off inside the US defense-education debate driven by AI and drones; signals institutional resistance to tech-first reforms.

themes.theme: Track record of failed RMA predictions

insights.claim: Jan Bloch declared in 1901 that new technologies made studying history useless; he correctly foresaw firepower and entrenchment making decisive battle impossible but wrongly predicted rational states would abandon war and that nations could not sustain modern war costs for more than a few months.
insights.speaker: Michael P. Ferguson and Clifford J. Rogers
insights.so_what: Tactical forecasts can be right while strategic conclusions are badly wrong — a caution against extrapolating technology trends to political outcomes.

insights.claim: Historical predictions that a new technology would transform war — Douhet's 1921 airpower thesis, Brodie's 1946 nuclear-deterrence argument just before Korea, and the 1990s 'system of systems' that failed to lift the fog of war in Afghanistan and Iraq — repeatedly proved wrong.
insights.speaker: Michael P. Ferguson and Clifford J. Rogers
insights.so_what: Skepticism toward claims that AI or drones will make war unrecognizable; defense-tech narratives may overshoot actual battlefield impact.
